ios.desc:
The camera roll was never designed for a lifetime. It's a scrolling nightmare: newest on top, everything else sinking out of sight. 

PhotoGather turns your album into a collage — all laid out on one infinite canvas for you to explore.

A Collage That (Mostly) Assembles Itself:

Bring in your photos and PhotoGather arranges them into little collages — a trip, a month, a moment — then gathers those into bigger ones, all the way up to your whole life.

• Photos arrange themselves — grouped by year, month, and moment, with bursts of nearly identical shots tucked neatly together.
• Add a personal touch — reorder, combine, and group until the collage fits your memories. Bring your favorites front and center.
• On-device AI — screenshots and documents are filtered away from your real memories, and each photo is automatically reframed on its subject.

Curate Once. Explore Forever:

Explore your infinite canvas with familiar pinch and zoom controls. Zoom in to the moments that matter, and stumble across the memories that you forgot.

Built for real lifetimes: libraries of 50,000+ photos stay smooth to arrange and explore.

Simple Pricing: 

Try everything free with your first 1,000 photos. PhotoGather Pro is a single one-time purchase that removes the photo limit. No subscription.

A photo you can't find is a memory you don't have. Start exploring today.

quotes.text:
I'm working on an iPhone app called PhotoGather. https://apps.apple.com/us/app/photogather/id6738232616

I've got 40k+ photos on my iphone, and wanted a better way to interact with them. The basic idea I had was to virtually stitch all the photos together into a gigapixel image, and navigate that image with pinch and zoom. On import, the app hierarchically groups photos based on date and similarity. The user can go back and edit the groups, change the layout, and adjust the size of photos if they choose.

The interesting I noticed is that in the process of curating and organizing my photos, I stumble across memories and moments that I had completely forgot.

Development Challenge: The app does two interesting things underneath the hood... First, given an arbitrary number of thumbnails with different aspect ratios, it finds the best sized rectangle that completely fits all the photos. This allows me to recursively stitch groups together and always output a rectangular thumbnail for the group. Second, the pinch/zoom UI uses these nested thumbnails directly without slicing/dicing to fixed sized tiles.
quotes.story_title: Ask HN: What are you working on? (November 2026)
